summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 85/113)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Ruq af femi, d lo qəlbət ʕal u xabrayḏox." Rəqle af feme lu malko, hulele i kəmme.
data.translation: "So spucke in meinen Mund, dass du dein Wort nicht brichst." Da spuckte der König in seinen Mund, und der Fuchs gab ihm die Mütze.

rationale: Imperativ in a pledge context; same literal act, with promise clause.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.14/154)

data.turoyo: An noše, i naqqa d maftalle ḥaṣayye l Məḏyaḏ, bdalle baṣ ṣuʕre li Ndaṯ Aloho, l Mšiḥo w saymiwo ṣlibo b ṣawʕoṯayye w rayqiwo aʕle. <...>
data.translation: The people, when they turned their backs toward Midyat, began insults against the Mother of God and Christ, and they were making a cross with their fingers and spitting on it. <...>

rationale: First Infectum-wa box after round 1; plural repeated spitting with ʕal-target, context gives the target's antecedent. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 78/74)

data.turoyo: Rəqla af feme, əmmo: "U maṭlaq d lišoni lu taʕlo w lo l nošo ḥreno."
data.translation: Da spie sie ihm in den Mund und sprach: "Die Macht meiner Zunge soll dem Fuchs gehören, und keinem andern."

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; overt feminine agent transfers power by mouth-spitting.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 78/78)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Mə kəbʕət, taʕlo?" Omər: "Mdaywalla l aṯti, huləxla u maṭlaq d lišonəx w lə rəqləx af fema."
data.translation: fragte sie: "Was begehrst du, Fuchs?" Er antwortete: "Meine Frau ist besessen geworden, denn du hast die Kraft deiner Zunge auf sie übertragen, ohne ihr in den Mund zu speien."

rationale: Second-person feminine Preterit in a negated clause adds person contrast.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (59/44)

data.turoyo: Li kurfo məlla: "Ya zʕuro, madam latlux haž mina, elux lo qṭilolux, amṭay, groyaqno b femux!"
data.translation: Die Schlange sprach: "Junge! Nachdem du nichts damit zu tun hast und du sie nicht getötet hast, komm mal her, damit ich dir in den Mund speie!"

rationale: Infectum has one existing example; first-person prospective spitting adds person/aspect contrast.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (59/49)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d rəqla b feme, yaləf bal lišone da ḥyewən, d kətne bi arʕo kulle.
data.translation: Als sie ihm in den Mund gespien hatte, konnte er auf einmal die Sprachen aller Tiere auf Erden.

rationale: Fifth Preterit example links actual spitting to knowledge acquisition; temporal anterior reading.

summary: Mouth destination alternates af fem- and b-fem-. No distinct sense is established by ritual power transfer, healing, oath confirmation or acquisition of animal languages: each context still describes literal spitting.

Preterit L-series endings encode the spitter even without a direct object. Goal and recipient are expressed through the mouth phrase. Infectum contrasts prospective groyaqno, conditional rayqət and habitual kroyəq.

The entry already quotes the fox healing his wife and habitual treatment; PrS 78/80 repeats those passages. The existing citation list also points to further Prym–Socin parallels, so equivalent healing quotations are not multiplied.
No conventional idiom is inferred merely from the narrative consequences of spitting; no light verb is present.
Round 1 supplies an Imperativ but no Infectum-wa; rayqiwo is therefore a genuine new box.
The construction still denotes literal spitting. ʕal-target complements the round-1 b-/af-mouth goals; no Detransitive or new religious sense is introduced.
Is mouth-spitting to bind a promise a conventional practice beyond PrS 85/113? The corpus does not establish a distinct lexical sense.
